urdu_nllb.PK001: Spread over four floors, including a partially covered roof, Clifton is a well-known resort that is almost always crowded, but people come so quickly that it's usually not necessary to book.
urdu_nllb.PK002: One of the oldest places in Karachi, it is home to pure indigenous food and slow-cooked barbecue that locals have trusted for decades.
urdu_nllb.PK003: A large clay-walled building where Pakistani buffets can be eaten openly, is popular enough to accommodate tourists as it also provides cleanliness along with local cuisine.
urdu_nllb.PK004: Built in the style of a 17th-century Mughal castle, the place offers brandy, barbecue and ale in an open brick courtyard and is quite crowded on weekends.
urdu_nllb.PK005: Right next to the stadium, there's a fully truck-driven atmosphere of sitting down on the chariot and drinking licorice; a variety of nanas, chicken moguls and mutton chaps are local favorites.
urdu_nllb.PK006: On the last floor of the seventeen-story tower, you'll find terraciki, tempura and spicy tuna tartar, as well as a 360-degree view of the city.
urdu_nllb.PK007: A well-known place in the diplomatic area where French cuisine is served in dimly lit rooms is somewhat expensive but the wine list is very extensive.
urdu_nllb.PK008: This large place near the center serves kaaba and Afghan specials and is packed with locals and foreigners for dinner.
urdu_nllb.PK009: Located on a hill above the city, it has an extensive list of cuisines and a beautiful atmosphere, but getting there is a mission and the rent is special.
urdu_nllb.PK010: A branch of the famous site of Sayedpur, located inside a large tent in E-11, offers the best Pakistani food but can be quiet on weekdays.
urdu_nllb.PK011: This award-winning, state-of-the-art venue offers about 139 Chinese dishes in a Chinese-style room and is quite popular with foreigners.
urdu_nllb.PK012: A magnificent place on Club Road where only buffet-style indigenous food is served, as well as live classical music every day.
urdu_nllb.PK013: It's owned by the same company that runs the clay village buffet, but there's a regular snack cart menu here; try their sweet lattes.
urdu_nllb.PK014: A state-of-the-art facility featuring almost all the best seafood and steaks, it's popular with the elite, and it's very crowded.
urdu_nllb.PK015: It serves special goat meat in a village-style manner with pulk and dates and is a favourite spot for both Inter-Subai truck drivers and locals alike.
urdu_nllb.PK016: The city's purest lunch is here; the marble bones in the thick black pepper gravy are the hallmark of the city, no reservations and the space fills up quickly.
urdu_nllb.PK017: An excellent high-end Pakistani and Afghan place with both Western-style seats and floor mats; always packing is a testament to its food.
urdu_nllb.PK018: A remarkable roof overlooking a small lake with flamingo birds and Greek statues, often featuring barbecue and curry, is popular with the city's middle class.
urdu_nllb.PK021: A small treasure where many people say there's better coffee than big chains, in a beautiful environment with a good range of authentic coffee and cakes.
urdu_nllb.PK022: Right next to a bank branch, a small and tasty pastry shop that's more suitable for lunch or coffee than dinner, and has a wide range of hot drinks.
urdu_nllb.PK023: A classic exotic coffee shop, usually expensive, with special decorations and items of Nordic design, is also for sale.
urdu_nllb.PK024: A beautiful open space where good continental food meets in a pleasant and artistic atmosphere.
urdu_nllb.PK025: An Irish chocolate maker runs this high and beautiful place where chocolates and gifts are served alongside drinks.
urdu_nllb.PK026: A comfortable room with a beautifully decorated interior where delicious coffee, desserts, and girls meet is a good place to spend time.
urdu_nllb.PK027: It's an artistic space about an hour from the city where there's jazz on Saturday nights and sufi nights on Tuesday nights; sitting inside feels almost like Venice.
urdu_nllb.PK030: A small, cozy indoor and outdoor-style room designed with simple, home-scented and well-served Asian and European cuisine in mind, especially for the expatriate class.
urdu_nllb.PK031: Mostly known for its Pratha roll, which wrapped fillings such as cheese, sauce, and garlic mayonnaise with chicken, beef, or cabbage; the simple roll is cheaper.
urdu_nllb.PK032: Standard fast food: stoneware, burgers, fries, shampoo, rolls, salads, pastries and soups.
urdu_nllb.PK033: A club-style venue known for its crispy fried chicken and pizza.
urdu_nllb.PK034: It is characterized by a two-stage barbecue method for ribs, located right in the busy area of the clock tower.
urdu_nllb.PK035: A Chinese company known for selling its famous brandy, it has branches throughout the city and has a large following among brandy enthusiasts.
urdu_nllb.PK036: A local chain of stalls that also offers fresh fruit juice and some good country shakes for every season.
urdu_nllb.PK037: A popular counter at the bottom of the restaurant where you get really fresh things like chocolate chip cookies, cheeseburgers and low-cholesterol items, made to order.
urdu_nllb.PK038: A specialty European-style business that makes specialty breads, cheesecakes and gelato, as well as an outdoor lawn for barbecue.
urdu_nllb.PK039: Very popular for its bakery items and generally considered the best pizza place in town, there is also a place to eat outdoors.
urdu_nllb.PK040: A beautiful place with a great little counter of custom-made cupcakes attached.
urdu_nllb.PK044: Built during the reign of the Mughal king Aurangzeb, it was for a long time the largest of its kind in the world; entrance is free and you have to take off your shoes in Delhi.
urdu_nllb.PK045: It is often said to be the largest single-domed building of its kind in the world, built in 1969 of white marble, with its 72-meter dome perched on a low wall without a pillar.
urdu_nllb.PK046: The capital's most recognizable symbol, a gift from a Saudi king; it's a place of worship far more serious than a tourist spot, and can be visited outside the hours of non-Muslim prayers.
urdu_nllb.PK047: Located near Delhi Gate, a beautiful tiled temple is famous for its brightly colored tiles on its surfaces.
urdu_nllb.PK048: It was commissioned by the governor of Peshawar in 1630 during the reign of Shah Jahan; it is still an active place of worship in the old city today.
urdu_nllb.PK049: A 17th-century prince gave it as a gift of thanks to refugees in exile, it is made of red brick and blue glossy tiles, has 93 domes, and was designed to be heard without the use of loudspeakers.
urdu_nllb.PK050: The oldest of its kind in Milan, it's now roofless and most of its blue-bright tiles have fallen into disrepair, but some parts are still intact.
urdu_nllb.PK051: There is a historic synagogue on the campus of the Islamic College.
urdu_nllb.PK052: The green dome enclosure on a hill overlooking Clifton Beach is attributed to a 9th-century Sufi elder who is believed to be the patron saint of the city; Thursday nights are often Qawwali and Christmas is celebrated every year.
urdu_nllb.PK053: A large modern building attributed to the city's patron saint, it is always packed with people who pray, give or take charity, or eat in a large free anchorage.
urdu_nllb.PK054: Nurpur is a monastery of a Sufi elder in the Valley of the Shahs, a historic shrine located on the edge of the capital.
urdu_nllb.PK055: In a village near the capital is the site of the Sufi elder Pir Meher Ali Shah, which is considered an important religious destination.
urdu_nllb.PK056: There's an 1800-year-old shrine on the side of a road.
urdu_nllb.PK060: Built in 1851, it is one of the few remaining Hindu temples in Peshawar.
urdu_nllb.PK061: The city's most popular and busiest Hindu temple belongs to a community founded by Swami Narayan; this large building was built in 1849.
urdu_nllb.PK063: Built in 1637 for Mughal king Jahangir, it is located in a walled garden across the river from the old city.
urdu_nllb.PK064: The final resting place of the Sikh ruler of Lahore is located right next to the square between the fort and the Great Mosque.
urdu_nllb.PK065: The white marble resting place of the country's founder, located on a high cliff, where the guards change every few hours and national days are celebrated.
urdu_nllb.PK068: The resting place of a chieftain of the Bombay tribe who united the hill tribes of the Kashmir-Hazara border and gave his name to the nearby city.
urdu_nllb.PK069: A tower, sometimes called the country's Eiffel Tower, was built on the site where the requirement for isolation was formally approved in 1940.
urdu_nllb.PK070: Near the sugar plantations, four flower-like walls represent provinces and territories; from the atmosphere, they create a starry halo, and inside there is a small museum and city view.
urdu_nllb.PK071: A tower built on a road square to commemorate the 1974 Islamic Summit, below which there is also a lesser-known library and museum in the square.
urdu_nllb.PK072: Built in 1919 by philanthropists as a promenade along the beach, it is now an ornamental landmark with a panoramic view of the surrounding park.
urdu_nllb.PK073: The 140-foot-tall cross, considered the tallest in Asia, stands at the entrance to the city's oldest and largest Christian cemetery.
urdu_nllb.PK074: A garden with a bitter political history: The country's first prime minister was assassinated here in 1951, and a former prime minister was assassinated here decades later.
urdu_nllb.PK076: An extensive walled enclosure where the Mughals and later Sikh rulers built their royal residences, it is now a World Heritage Site, and inside is a small museum of the 18th century Sikh era.
urdu_nllb.PK077: Built on a hill above the town in the 16th century, the castle has witnessed several wars, the last being in 1948, when the Indus River flows just below its walls.
urdu_nllb.PK078: The only remaining remains of the castle, which once stood on a high clay ridge and whose walls were about 1 mile (1.6 km) long; it was destroyed by the British army, and now part of the site is a park with British-era monuments.
urdu_nllb.PK079: One of the most historic sites in Peshawar, whose Persian name means 'high castle'; a Chinese Zayr who passed here in 630 AD mentioned a royal residence here.
urdu_nllb.PK080: An attempt to combine the shape of a medieval castle like Rohatas with a playground, it also hosts exhibitions and horse and cattle shows every year.
urdu_nllb.PK081: An ancient settlement in Sindh dating back to around 3600 BC.
urdu_nllb.PK082: The city was built by a Greek-Bactrian king who invaded the area in about 180 B.C.E. and established an Indo-Greek empire that lasted for nearly two centuries.
urdu_nllb.PK083: A world heritage-listed Buddhist monastery complex, dating back to the first century B.C.
urdu_nllb.PK084: One of the most important remnants of the Hindu era, a sun-worshiping site mentioned in many ancient books, is no longer visible on earth.
urdu_nllb.PK085: Locally known as the 'House of the Clock', a landmark of the old city's colonial period whose square was recently renovated.
urdu_nllb.PK086: Built in 1900 to commemorate Queen Victoria's Diamond Jubilee and named after a British provincial governor.
urdu_nllb.PK087: Built in 1892 to commemorate a Sindh commissioner, the 35-meter-tall building with a round clock was constructed in the Gothic Revival style of brown translucent stone.
urdu_nllb.PK089: The famous formal entrance to the castle, opposite the Great Mosque, has two pillars that are said to resemble elephant feet.
urdu_nllb.PK090: Decorated with colorful tiles, the locals call it the 'Elephant Gate' because it was once the entrance to the royal elephants, with a wide stairway built for the elephant's footsteps.
urdu_nllb.PK091: A magnificent, ornate four-towered building from 1646, which once served as a gateway to the walled city.
urdu_nllb.PK092: It got its name because it is in the direction of Delhi and the road leading to it; in the Mughal era, kings and state guests entered the city through the same road.
urdu_nllb.PK093: It got its name from the ironworkers who lived outside this gate of the old city wall for a long time and ran their shops.
urdu_nllb.PK094: The capital's largest collection, more than 25 galleries in four connected buildings covering architecture, textiles, musical heritage and Sufi shrines, as well as a reference library and crafts sales center.
urdu_nllb.PK095: A lesser-known place to look for a magnificent day trip on the North Western Railway: a renovated station house where you can see a small collection and old engines.
urdu_nllb.PK096: The largest institution of its kind in the country, founded in 1864 during the British era, reflects the region's culture, as well as its magnificent collection of Gandhara Buddhist art.
urdu_nllb.PK097: There is a 20 million-year-old hand-held skull overlooking the Pothohar Plateau, 18,000 old coins, hundreds of sculptures, and the remains of Mohenjo-Doo, including a statue of the famous 'Priest-King'.
urdu_nllb.PK098: An open exhibition established in 1990 with more than 30 aircraft, weapons and radars housed in a large green park, as well as an indoor hall with fighter jets used in wars with India.
urdu_nllb.PK099: Six galleries and an auditorium on the theme of maritime and maritime heritage, displayed via diorama, sculptor and touchscreen, with a retired submarine and a military aircraft outside.
urdu_nllb.PK100: The country's only currency collection, which shows financial history from the English era to the present day in seven galleries.
urdu_nllb.PK101: The country's first interactive science centre, opened in 2021, with over 200 hands-on exhibits, is built in an old colonial railway warehouse, outside the Science Garden.
urdu_nllb.PK102: Once the private home of painter Shakur Ali, it was purchased after his death and opened in 1976 to preserve his work and showcase a combination of modern and traditional architecture.
urdu_nllb.PK104: Completed in 1865, the two-story family home where the country's founders were born and raised; it is a protected monument with a reading hall and galleries of their personal belongings.
urdu_nllb.PK107: In the shadow of a colonial-era Gothic-Mongol clock house, the 1889 building is built around a courtyard and has about 280 shops where everything from fruit, meat to clothing and pets is found.
urdu_nllb.PK108: Rawalpindi's oldest and most traditional trading area: a street famous for clothing and imitation jewelry, the second most famous gold market in the city.
urdu_nllb.PK109: One of the cheapest shopping spots in the city, the forgotten shops where handicrafts and simple clothing are found, including locally made export surplus brands.
urdu_nllb.PK110: A palace named Mossom that was buried alive for loving the prince, a forgotten alleyway where almost everything from handicrafts to radio and women's clothing can be found.
urdu_nllb.PK111: A one-dimensional commercial warehouse where more than a hundred plant and animal oils are found, a spice street, a clothing section and separate streets for bedding and sleeping.
urdu_nllb.PK112: The main commercial centre and oldest part of Faisalabad, a central clock house, has eight markets arranged in the shape of a Union Jack in the British era.
urdu_nllb.PK113: A lively pedestrian street, sometimes closed to vehicles, where you can buy gifts such as essential items or jewelry and also bring local stamps.
urdu_nllb.PK115: One of the oldest presidential chambers of commerce, it houses a wide variety of items, from clothing to electronics, and is also a great place for traditional gifts, carpets and handicrafts.
urdu_nllb.PK116: The largest of its kind in the city, it also has clothing, a few restaurants, a currency exchange and a small bookstore.
urdu_nllb.PK117: One of the three Chinese branches in the city, it is located just off the coast and competes with Dubai's luxury locations, with well-known brand stores, a hypermarket and a large food court.
urdu_nllb.PK118: One of the city's oldest high-end shopping areas, it's still bustling, with boutiques, food courts, supermarkets, an indoor children's park and an art gallery.
urdu_nllb.PK119: A multi-storey space with escalators, bright floors, and plenty of clothing shops, it's a comfortable alternative in the summer when open markets are hot.
urdu_nllb.PK120: There are over a thousand men's formal wear shops here, offering a wide selection at reasonable prices.
urdu_nllb.PK121: First built for exhibition and later used for commerce, the 1864 building now houses the city's cultural heritage collection.
urdu_nllb.PK123: Also known as F-9 and considered one of the largest green spaces in South Asia, it is good for jogging, cricket grounds, tennis courts, a large playground for children and indoor bowling alley.
urdu_nllb.PK125: Built on a hill, it offers views of the city from above and is a popular picnic spot, with leisure rides, dining and an artificial lake.
urdu_nllb.PK126: Opened in 2007 and built to commemorate an eighth-century victor, it's the largest family green space in South Asia, with some ponds, stone umbrellas and millions of rose bushes.
urdu_nllb.PK127: Along Canal Road to the east of the city, there is a large 450-acre drive-in green space with a drive-in zoo, an artificial lake, a small museum and a complex of water rides.
urdu_nllb.PK128: With vast meadows, a boating lake and a well-maintained jogging track, a huge green space, it also hosts flower shows in spring.
urdu_nllb.PK129: It covers about 2,300 acres and includes a playground, a boating lake, an aquarium, a garden restaurant, and an open-air theater.
urdu_nllb.PK130: A sophisticated green space with special themes  Japanese, palm, rose and cactus gardens  Here is an artist's corner, a small library and a 3 km clay jogging track with light music.
urdu_nllb.PK132: A viewpoint in the hills above the city from which you can see far away on a clear day, with flowers on its slopes, and nearby hiking trails, restaurants and live music.
urdu_nllb.PK133: The three-tiered ceremonial Mughal layout, built in the 1600s, including waterways and waterfalls, is on the World Heritage List.
urdu_nllb.PK134: Two quiet lawns on either side of a colonial building, including old Victorian fountains, are locally known as the Garden of Gethsemane.
urdu_nllb.PK135: A quiet rural sanctuary surrounding an artificial lake, with a brick pavilion and a tower built by a Mughal king on his pet deer grave.
urdu_nllb.PK136: On the north side of the reservoir, a beautifully built site with gardens, picnic areas and secretive trails, there is now a bird sanctuary, go-kart tracks and climbing walls.
urdu_nllb.PK137: On the edge of the capital, a forested, mountainous, green and natural environment is a good place for peaceful evening walks.
urdu_nllb.PK138: Established in 1872, one of the oldest places of its kind on the continent, it attracts a large number of visitors throughout the year.
urdu_nllb.PK139: Established in 1878, formerly known as the Mahatma Gandhi Garden, there are about 107 cages housing hundreds of species of birds, mammals and reptiles, along with a Mughal-style garden and a small aquarium.
urdu_nllb.PK140: Opened in 1970 for families only, it has a few animal collections, a children's playground, gardens and a chair lift to view the animals from above.
urdu_nllb.PK142: An artificial part of the water where pedal boats are rented and there are also some electric swingers, sometimes there's a walking carnival.
urdu_nllb.PK143: Staff can arrange a shared jeep for safety from here, and you can also pick up breakfast from across the street.
urdu_nllb.PK144: The Margalla hills overlook the capital, which can be reached in about 40 minutes by road or about two hours by footpath, with two dining areas at the top.
urdu_nllb.PK148: Along with the harbour, a pedestrian-friendly strip with dozens of restaurants and stalls, including an art gallery, a mosque, a children's play area and a stage, allows only families and couples to enter.
urdu_nllb.PK151: 20 storey building, the tallest of its kind in the country, with 236 rooms and suites, tennis courts, swimming pool and fitness center with sauna.
urdu_nllb.PK152: The best place to stay in the capital, with five stars, good restaurants and a gym.
urdu_nllb.PK153: Once one of the top places to stay, it was destroyed by a truck bomb explosion in 2008, rebuilt in three months and reopened with strict security.
urdu_nllb.PK154: A beautiful little place to stay in a lush residential sector, with a spectacular view of private terraces and the Margalla hills.
urdu_nllb.PK155: Between the tropical gardens and palm trees, there is a mid-sized resort with a view of the creek and the sea, 82 rooms, free Wi-Fi and four restaurants including a floating restaurant.
urdu_nllb.PK156: Popular with backpackers, the private rooms here are surrounded by a beautiful garden courtyard and a small kitchen serves good food, with a dormitory added in 2019 and secure parking.
urdu_nllb.PK157: The original magnificent old residence in Lahore was built by an Italian in the late 18th century and later renovated.
urdu_nllb.PK158: Named after a villain of a series of historical novels, apparently run by the government and set in the middle of the city.
urdu_nllb.PK159: A quiet shelter among the cedars with restaurants, bars, billiards rooms and several separate cottages in a quiet corner of the compound.
urdu_nllb.PK160: Expensive but comfortable and air-conditioned, this is probably the place to stay when the temperature drops to 47 degrees.
urdu_nllb.PK161: Opened in 1955 with a capacity of 50,000, it also hosts international Test matches and a T20 franchise team match.
urdu_nllb.PK162: Built in 1959 and renovated in 1996, with 27,000 seats, it is the home ground of international Test matches and Lahore's T20 team.
urdu_nllb.PK165: Rudyard Kipling's father was the principal here; there's a doctoral show here every winter, and there's a famous old cannon outside the gate.
urdu_nllb.PK166: An old, traditional campus building built on the central square project, with lines reflecting Islamic architecture.
urdu_nllb.PK168: The only five star place to stay in Faisalabad with three restaurants and an outdoor swimming pool.
urdu_nllb.PK174: A small replica of London's famous Traveller's Landmark, including its central pillar, is on the outskirts of Navy Town, along with a miniature Egypt and a small zoo nearby.
urdu_nllb.PK178: A traditionally decorated Old Town neighborhood in which an influential family built seven Central Asian-style mansions in the late 19th century, some of which are open to visitors and feature intricate wood carvings.

roman_llm.PK001: Clifton area: This place is spread over 4 floors, and one of the floors has a half-covered terrace. It's always packed, but the turnover is so fast that you don't really need reservations.
roman_llm.PK002: There is an old place in Karachi where people can find authentic desi cuisine and slow-cooked BBQ, which has earned the trust of the locals.
roman_llm.PK003: There is a very big area covered in earth and surrounded by walls where you can find an all-you-can-eat Pakistani buffet. Tourists like to come here because they also get local food and the cleanliness is reliable.
roman_llm.PK004: It is built in the style of a 17th century Mughal fort, featuring an open brick courtyard where you can enjoy biryani, BBQ, and haleem, and it gets quite busy on weekends.
roman_llm.PK005: Sitting on a mat right next to the stadium, you get the vibe of a truck driver; naan, chicken mughlai, and mutton chops are the local favorites here.
roman_llm.PK006: On the top floor of a 17-story tower, you get teriyaki, tempura, and spicy tuna tartare, along with a 360-degree city view.
roman_llm.PK007: The diplomatic enclave has a social scene where you can enjoy French food in dimly lit rooms, it's a bit pricey but the wine list is quite extensive.
roman_llm.PK008: Near the center, this large place serves kebabs and Afghan specialties, and it's filled with locals and expats during dinner time.
roman_llm.PK009: In the city above, you can find a variety of cuisines and a lovely ambiance, but getting there feels like an adventure and it’s also quite a trek.
roman_llm.PK010: Saidpur is just one of the popular places, located on E-11 inside a large tent where you can find delicious Pakistani food, but it might be a bit empty during weekdays.
roman_llm.PK011: Award-winning and upscale place, offering around 139 Chinese dishes in a Chinese-style decorated room, and it's quite popular among expats.
roman_llm.PK012: On Club Road, there's a place for fine dining, while Indian cuisine is only available buffet-style and there's live classical music every day.
roman_llm.PK013: Mitti wale village buffet-style company has only one location, but they do offer a proper a-la-carte menu here; you should definitely try their sweet lassi.
roman_llm.PK014: There is an upscale place where you can find almost every type of high-quality seafood and steaks, and it's popular among the elite crowd, so it can get quite busy.
roman_llm.PK015: In this village-style setting, the menu includes special mutton cooked with spinach and lentils. Both inter-province truck drivers and locals enjoy it.
roman_llm.PK016: The most authentic lunch in the city can be found here; lamb joints in thick black-pepper gravy are their specialty, and you don't need to make a reservation as it fills up quickly.
roman_llm.PK017: There is an amazing upscale place in Pakistan and Afghanistan where both Western-style seating and floor cushions are available; it's always packed during meals.
roman_llm.PK018: There is a small lake side area with a nostalgic roof where flamingos and Greek statues can be seen, with more BBQ and curries available, and it is popular among the city's middle class.
roman_llm.PK021: There is a small gem of a place where many people say they get better coffee than big chains, in a pleasant atmosphere with a good range of proper coffee and cakes.
roman_llm.PK022: Right next to the bank branch, there is a small and pleasant pastry shop that is more suitable for lunch or coffee, and it offers a wide range of hot drinks.
roman_llm.PK023: An expat-friendly spot for classic coffee, commonly visited, where you can also find exclusive decor items and some Nordic design pieces.
roman_llm.PK024: There is a nice open-air spot where you can get good continental food, and the atmosphere is also artistic and pleasant.
roman_llm.PK025: An Irish chocolatier operates in this upscale, elegant place where you can also get chocolates and gifts along with drinks.
roman_llm.PK026: A cozy room is available with good interior, gourmet coffee, desserts, and grills. It's a great spot for hanging out.
roman_llm.PK027: There is a place within a kilometer of the city that offers an artistic atmosphere where you can enjoy jazz on Saturday nights and Sufi music on Tuesday nights; sitting there gives you almost a feeling like being in Venice.
roman_llm.PK030: In a small, cozy inside-outside room, you can find simple, home-style and well-presented Asian and European cuisine, specifically targeted at the expat crowd.
roman_llm.PK031: It is more famous for its own paratha roll, which includes chicken, beef, or kebab along with cheese, chutney, and garlic mayonnaise; the plain one is cheaper.
roman_llm.PK032: Quality quick eats include: pathooray, burgers, fries, shawarma, roll paratha, salads, pasta, and soups.
roman_llm.PK033: There's a spot that's known for its crispy fried chicken and pizza.
roman_llm.PK034: Her specialty ribs use a two-step BBQ process, right in the area near the clock tower.
roman_llm.PK035: There is a chain that is known for selling famous biryani, and it has branches all over the city. It has quite a following among biryani lovers.
roman_llm.PK036: Local chain stores where you can get fresh juice of seasonal fruits, and some good milkshakes as well.
roman_llm.PK037: Below the restaurant, there is a popular counter where many fresh items are available, such as chocolate fudge cake, cheesecake, and low-cholesterol items, which they prepare upon order.
roman_llm.PK038: A place that specializes in European-style baked goods, such as special breads, cheesecakes, and gelatos, and also has regular BBQ outdoors on the lawn.
roman_llm.PK039: Because of her baking skills, she is very popular and is often considered the best place for pizza in the city, as well as a spot to sit outside.
roman_llm.PK040: There's a small counter attached to which a little setup for making cupcakes in order with a swish (smooth) feel.
roman_llm.PK044: During the time of Mughal Emperor Aurangzeb, this place with its large rear area became one of the largest spots of its kind in the world; entry is free and people can remove their shoes here.
roman_llm.PK045: It claims to be the largest single-dome structure of its kind in the world, built in 1969 using white marble, and its 72-meter dome is directly applied to a lower wall without any pillars.
roman_llm.PK046: The most recognizable landmark of the government complex is a gift from a Saudi king; this is more of a place for serious worship than a tourist spot, and non-Muslims can also enter during prayer times.
